Subject: PayWell TCO & Pilot alignment — next steps

Hi Amir / Jenna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to make the next steps explicit: 

Top pain points you shared
- Token spend is the single biggest growth line item; unpredictable spikes during peak flows hurt margins.
- Latency spikes (>200ms p95) on the fraud-check path are triggering false positives and manual reviews.
- Engineering capacity is limited for building and operating an on-prem inference stack.

Primary goals we heard
- Reduce per-request inference cost by 30–50% within 90 days of pilot completion.
- Achieve p99 latency <200ms (target p95 <150ms) for the fraud-check microservice.
- Validate a deployment model (hosted vs dedicated vs private) that meets security and cost constraints.

Token economics (sketch) — please see attached PayWell_TCO_Model.xlsx for the working numbers
Assumptions (example baseline)
- Monthly traffic: 5M inference requests
- Avg tokens per request: 120 (prompt + completion)
- Current provider blended cost: $0.0045/token (internal estimation)

Projected unit-cost ranges (illustrative)
- Redwood Hosted (managed): $0.0028–$0.0036/token depending on model choice and batching
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved): $0.0019–$0.0027/token with small reserved GPU pool and persistent KV cache
- Redwood Private (customer-managed infra): $0.0016–$0.0024/token but higher upfront ops/integration effort

Pilot proposal (6 weeks) — high level- Objective: Demonstrate 30–50% unit-cost reduction on the fraud-check path while meeting latency targets.
- Scope: 2-week baseline (traffic capture, baseline metrics) + 4-week optimization run (batching, prefix caching, quantization tests).
- Deliverables: weekly econ readout, latency SLO dashboard, small SOW + rollback plan.
- Success criteria: >=30% cost reduction OR p99 latency improvement to <200ms with no >5% accuracy regression on evaluation set.

Mutual action plan (MAP) — next 10 business days
1) Redwood: deliver a draft SOW and pilot config (attached) — target: Thu 7/6
2) PayWell: confirm pilot budget range and legal/compliance contacts — target: Fri 7/7
3) Both: align on dataset and evaluation prompts for quality checks — target: Mon 7/10

Budget framing
- Rough pilot estimate: $40k–$75k depending on Dedicated vs Hosted and the amount of reserved capacity.
- Typical payback: customers with high QPS and long-running sessions often see payback within 2–3 months post-rollout when batching/kv caching stabilize.

Attachments: PayWell_TCO_Model.xlsx (working numbers), redwood-pilot-SOW-draft.pdf (outline)

Could you confirm: 1) the 90-day ROI requirement you mentioned (is that firm?), 2) whether you prefer Redwood Dedicated for predictable unit-costs or want a Hosted proof-of-value first?

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30-minute kick-off next week to lock the MAP and finalize SOW.

Thanks —

— Soojin

Thanks Soojin — good summary and yes, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: our procurement has a firm allotment of $60k for Q3 specifically for vendor pilots that can demonstrate cost-savings. We can stretch to $80k if there’s a clear path to dedicated capacity that drives immediate savings.
- ROI timeline: we need to see a path to payback within 3 months after pilot completion. That doesn’t mean full rollout in 3 months, but the math should show payback <90 days with our projected traffic.
- Security/compliance: we can do Hosted for the pilot, but any production rollout will need to live in a VPC; SOC2 evidence and an audit trail will be required before prod.

On metrics: we can provide historical traffic traces (anonymized) and a curated evaluation set for the fraud-check path.

Next steps for us: please send the SOW and detailed cost scenarios (Hosted vs Dedicated) — we’ll route to procurement and legal the moment we have a draft.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I’ve copied Jenna who will own procurement logistics.

— Amir

Marissa — forwarding Amir’s reply (below). Key asks: firm $60k pilot budget, 3-month payback requirement, SOC2 evidence for production. Jenna is procurement owner.

My recommended approach for the pilot (internal notes):
- Start with Hosted proof-of-value for 4 weeks (captures baseline, validates batching/kv cache gains) then transition to a small Dedicated pool for the last 2 weeks to measure sustained unit-cost with reserved capacity. This lets us reduce integration risk while showing both Hosted and Dedicated economics.
- Pilot config: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs in dedicated pool (for the Dedicated window), KV cache warmed from captured traffic, batching window tuned to 40–80ms for fraud path to balance latency and throughput.
- Cost estimate (rough, based on our internal cost model + PayWell assumptions):
  * Hosted PoV (4 weeks): ~$18k–$28k (includes managed infra + engineering support)
  * Dedicated validation (2 weeks): incremental $22k–$34k (reserved capacity + burst buffer)
  * Total pilot: $40k–$62k (fits Amir’s $60k target depending on config)

Actions for us
1) I’ll update the SOW to reflect a two-stage pilot and include a short clause for SOC2 evidence request and audit window. Target SOW update: EOD Wed 7/4.
2) Marissa — can you own the finance check and confirm we can sign a pilot up to $62k under the solutions team credits? If not, what’s the internal approval path?
3) I’ll prepare a short evaluation harness (synthetic + their anonymized traces) and a dashboard template to track p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.

Risks to flag: if PayWell’s average tokens/request drops significantly in testing (they mentioned variable prompts), our batching benefits may be reduced — we’ll include sensitivity ranges in the SOW.

If you agree I’ll reply to Amir with the updated MAP, SOW link, and propose Wed 7/12 for a 30-min kick-off.

— Soojin
